newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to back renewal of Iraq oil-for-food program.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to back renewal of Iraq oil-for-food program.

text.p: The United States will support renewal of the United Nations' oil-for-food programme for Iraq, the State Department said on Tuesday.

"The secretary (of State Madeleine Albright) has decided that the United States will support the renewal of U.N. resolution 986 and that is the oil for food deal," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
"This agreement benefits the people of Iraq, as it should. It does not benefit in any way the government of Iraq, which does not deserve international support," Burns said.

U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan has recommended that the oil-for-food deal, which went into effect last December, be renewed for six months. It temporarily waives a U.N. ban on oil sales imposed after Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Under the humanitarian waiver, Iraq is allowed to sell up to $2 billion worth of oil in order to get money to buy food and medicine.
Most members of the U.N. Security Council, which must approve renewal of the deal, have said they would like to see the agreement approved under current terms or even increased.
